item.title: Frostbite: A new CPU architecture discovered, designed and verified by AI
item.description:
📝 Frostbite exploits the properties of interaction nets, namely that every step is local, every dependency is explicit, and every value has exactly one owner, to reach a step-function gain in CPU performance that has long stagnated. This forces CPUs to maintain the illusion that every core sees the same memory, and keeping that illusion consistent and performant requires deep cache hierarchies and coherence protocols that cost area and power, and scale poorly. Interaction nets1 take a different approach.
🔗 Read more: https://architectlabs.com/blog/frostbite

item.title: UK fridges secured from hackers in secret nationwide operation
item.description:
📝 "From a business perspective it could have been potentially devastating with business interruption and supply chain problems. Our warehouses have millions of pounds worth of food that could have been spoiled if any hackers found out about this method of attack," they added. There have been three waves of hacks on refrigeration temperature controllers so far this year:In August, fridges at a small number of US military bases were impactedOn 11 and 12 October hundreds of supermarkets and food processing sites in France were hit when Danfoss temperature control systems were targetedOn 1 and 2 November dozens of supermarkets across seven European countries were hit, with Belgium and Luxembourg the worst affected.
🔗 Read more: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c6eq49zyx7p4o
